title: The #1 QB recruit lost his NFL job to his own classmate

slide.small: Same recruiting class. Same NFL team.

lines: The number one quarterback recruit in 2015 lost his NFL job to his own classmate.
And the way it happened is wild.
Josh Rosen was the top QB in the whole class.
Five stars, a 4.3 GPA, and a former top junior tennis player.
At UCLA he started as a true freshman and broke the school's single-season passing record.
Then Arizona took him tenth overall in 2018.
Now meet the number three QB in that same class, Kyler Murray.
He went 43 and 0 as a high school starter and won three state titles.

slide.small: Also a first-round MLB draft pick

lines: He transferred to Oklahoma, won the Heisman, and got drafted in the first round of the MLB draft too.

slide.small: Arizona drafts Kyler. Rosen is traded to Miami.

lines: In 2019, just one year after drafting Rosen, Arizona took Kyler first overall, and traded Rosen to Miami.
Rosen bounced around the league and was out of the NFL after 2022.
He went to Wharton and reportedly moved into finance.
Kyler became Rookie of the Year and a two-time Pro Bowler, and in 2026 he's with the Minnesota Vikings.
Follow for part two: what happened to the rest of the 2015 class.
